subject: aftf
title: (R)AFTF.------TH.CONT.
description: Diagram in CMOA(I)-9 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — Britain/Germany/Holland) accompanying Braxton's claim about the post-Webern movement and the early-fifties emergence of European improvisation: 'the creativity which I have been experiencing in the last ten years can clearly be looked at as a separate creative thrust that is distinctly European in its vibrational identity and directly coupled to the challenge of world music.' (R)AFTF (the reality of affinity transfer) is crossed with TH-CONT (thrust continuance): the question is what affinity-transfer produces in its actual instantiation when crossed with thrust-continuance — under conditions where Europe is forging a creative identity distinct from American improvised music. TH-CONT sits at the upper-center. From TH-CONT a line runs down to T-C-IMP (time continuum implications), which carries TF-SH (transfer shift) on the upper-right. CRTF-D (cross-transfer definitions) hangs on the lower-right via a solid edge from T-C-IMP. POL-SIGN (political significance) anchors the bottom via a *dashed* edge from T-C-IMP — a dotted line that, in Braxton's legend, 'amplifies some aspect of the main concept it is connected to'. Structural argument: affinity-transfer-as-real crossed with thrust-continuance branches through time-continuum-implications as central hub.
